sources.entry: A feature toggle in software development provides an alternative to maintaining multiple feature branches in source code.

summary.name: Feature toggle
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article describing feature toggles, a software technique that uses runtime conditions to enable or disable features as an alternative to maintaining multiple feature branches.
use_cases: Releasing unfinished features hidden from users
Running canary releases to a small user cohort
Disabling a feature at runtime during an incident
Merging incomplete work into the main branch
summary.what_it_does: The page explains that a feature toggle is a condition in code that enables or disables a feature at runtime, so unfinished work can be merged into the main branch without appearing to users. It describes uses in continuous delivery, canary rollouts and A/B testing, and notes that toggles are often implemented as variables in conditional statements. It covers toggle types (release, business, experiment, ops, permissioning) and storage options such as database rows, config file properties, or external flag services. It also warns that toggles left in code long term create maintenance overhead and dead code.
notable: Describes release, business, experiment, ops and permissioning toggle types
Covers toggle debt and cleanup practices from academic studies
Lists large sites reported to use feature toggles, such as Flickr, Netflix and Gmail
caveats: Toggles left in code long term add maintenance burden and dead code
Page notes it may contain excessive references to self-published sources and some sections need more citations
